And yet this tribe, for the generality, were asinus osseus {Gen 49:14} dull, and desirous of peace.
paragraphs.anchor: They were valiant men of might.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The son; for it is likely that Uzzi had more sons, but nothing so famous as was Izrahiah.
Though they affected peace, as 1Ch 7:2, yet they were apti et parati ad bellum, ready pressed for war.
paragraphs.anchor: Were bands of soldiers for war.

paragraphs.text: Polygamy passed for current in the Church, because Abraham used it; though directly against the institution, and that plain law, {Lev 18:18} neither was it cast out of the Church till the captivity of Babylon.
paragraphs.anchor: For they had many wives and sons.

paragraphs.text: Omnes Iscariotae, saith Vatablus.

The genealogies of Dan and Zebulon are left out, for causes unknown; haply, because at their return out of Babylon their genealogies were not found. Dan is also - for their apostasy, likely, and idolatry - not reckoned among the rest that were sealed. {Rev 7:5-8} That Antichrist should be one of this tribe, is a fiction rightly exploded. We read of Hushim, {1Ch 7:12} the sons of Aher, which signifieth Another - and so some render it - by Another, understanding Dan, {compare Gen 46:23} whom the penman of this book held not worth the naming. The Hebrews, when they would show their detestation of any person or thing, they call it acher; a sow they call dabshar acher, that is, another thing; so leaven at the passover, &c. {a}
{a} Elias Thisbit.

The Ephraimites were famous for their wealth, power, and prowess; but withal they are noted for insolent, proud, and quarrelsome. See Jdg 8:1; Jdg 12:1.

Whom the men of Gath … slew.] And no marvel; because, belike, being weary of the Egyptian servitude, and remembering that Palestina was promised to their forefathers for an inheritance, they would needs take possession thereof before the time, which rash adventure of these sons of Ephraim cost them their lives, and perhaps occasioned that cruel decree of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, against the Israelites. {Exo 1:9-11} See to this purpose, Psa 78:9. This happened about the birth of Aaron. It is not safe to break God’s prison.
Who must needs be now a very old man.
His grief was the greater, if they went against the Gittites without his consent, as many young men are headlong and headstrong, &c.
The Benjamites also set upon the men of Gath, and took their city from them. {1Ch 8:13} Atque sic ulti sunt fratres suos Ephraemitas.
paragraphs.anchor: And his brethren came to comfort him.

paragraphs.text: A modest expression of the marriage duty. The apostle forbiddeth filthy speaking; {Eph 4:25; Eph 4:29; Eph 5:4} so doth Cicero, in his "Offices," inveighing against the Cynics for their obscene language.
paragraphs.anchor: And when he went in to his wife.

paragraphs.text: Of whom came a large offspring. This was a great mercy to the good old man.

A gallant woman, famous in her generation for beautifying and fortifying of sundry cities. Thus also God made up Ephraim’s loss.
The Vulgate calleth her Sarah; as likewise that other eminent woman. {1Ch 7:23}
